_about: Audit gates read by scripts/audit_video.py. This file is the single source of truth for every number the audit enforces; the rules files refer to gates by name. level: fail = fix before sharing, warn = look and decide.

integrated_lufs.why: Web and YouTube playback sits around -14 LUFS. YouTube turns loud uploads down but never turns quiet ones up (a reviewed cut sat at -20).

true_peak_dbtp.why: Headroom for the platform's lossy re-encode; stops inter-sample clipping.

clipped_samples.why: Any clipped sample is audible distortion.

loudest_moment_lu.why: The loudest 400 ms moment above the film's average loudness. A logo 'boom' rejected in review sat ~10 dB over the rest; accepted mixes peak at +5 to +6 LU. Keep sound effects within a few dB of the bed.

stereo_width.why: Side/mid RMS. Produced music is stereo (a catalog piano bed measured 0.30); the MusicGen-small bed measured 0.04, which sounds small and cheap.

air_db.why: Share of energy at 8-16 kHz. Below this the music sounds dull and closed-in (catalog piano -31 dB; MusicGen-small bed -41 dB). Run the audit on the music file alone, since clicks and whooshes in a full mix hide it.

video_mbps_1080p.why: YouTube's recommended upload bitrate for 1080p SDR at 24-30 fps (support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171). A proxy only: mostly-static UI encodes far below it even near-lossless (a CRF 8 4K product film measured 8.9 Mbps). Render the master at --crf 8 and judge 100% crops; a lossy low-CRF-quality encode (a reviewed cut: 0.46 Mbps at default CRF) is the real failure.

video_mbps_2160p.why: YouTube's recommended upload bitrate for 4K SDR at 24-30 fps. A proxy only: static UI legitimately encodes lower at near-lossless CRF (8.9 Mbps at CRF 8). Render at --crf 8 and check 100% crops instead of padding bitrate.

sparse_share.why: Share of frames showing only text or a logo on an empty stage, or nothing. Above ~15% a product video reads as a slide deck (a reviewed cut: 0.54).

first_rich_s.why: The product, or the problem in the product, should be on screen within 3 s; the opening seconds decide who keeps watching (a reviewed cut: 10.6 s).

longest_still_s.why: Nothing moving for more than ~5 s feels stalled. The final end-card hold may exceed it; anything mid-film should not.

length_off.why: Land within 10% of the brief's length. Retime by editing shots and holds, never by speeding up the whole film.

_manual_checks: One story: one customer or order, one problem, one cause, one fix, and the proof shown in the same view as the problem.
phone.png: every word and number the story depends on can be read at phone size.
No text, title or breadcrumb is sliced by a crop edge; product shots are at most ~25% empty.
The cursor is visible in every shot where it acts, and every click reads (click ring or a UI reaction).
Look and copy match the brand profile, and the end card has the URL plus one call to action, held at least 2 s.
The music fits the mood, sits under the picture, starts and ends cleanly, and has no time-stretch warble.
No global speed change was applied after rendering.
Every scene holds up next to its matching moment in the quality-bar reference (rules/quality-bar.md).
